0.27.0: **A page section lays out by the width of the `nldd-page` it is in, and goes nowhere else.** `nldd-simple-section`, `nldd-full-bleed-section`, `nldd-sidebar-section`, the three column sections and `nldd-hero` were each a container of their own. They now query the page, which they always span, by its container name `page-container`, so a card, container or other container of your own between them does not count. A section outside an `nldd-page` loses its responsive padding and columns, and a section in a narrower box inside the page lays out for the page. An `@container` query in your own CSS for content in a section no longer matches the section: it matches the page now, or the nearest container of your own. Put every section directly in a page, next to the other sections; `nldd lint` warns about both (see Added).

**`nldd-list-item` is no longer a container.** Its cells already lay out by the `nldd-list` around it. A component with container queries of its own in a row, such as `nldd-progress-bar`, now measures the list, which is as wide as the row. An `@container` query in your own CSS for content in a row matches the list now, or the nearest container of your own.

**`nldd-top-navigation-bar` follows the width of the window, not that of its parent.** The bar always spans the page, so the two were the same, and a media query costs the browser nothing per bar where a container query made every resize slower with each bar. A bar in a narrower box, such as a frame in your own docs, now lays out for the window it is in: give it an `iframe` of its own to show it narrow. An `@container` query in your own CSS for content in the bar no longer matches the bar.
0.26.3: **`nldd-popover` hides an `nldd-top-title-bar` in it on md and up.** Anchored beside its trigger, a popover closes with Escape or a click outside it, so the bar only matters on sm, where the popover is a bottom sheet. This holds for a bar anywhere in the popover, also in the header of an `nldd-page`. The bar in the pickers of `nldd-date-field` and in the overflow of `nldd-avatar-group` now shows on sm only, as it already did in `nldd-time-field`. Set `md-title-bar` on the popover to keep a bar whose dismiss button does what nothing else in the popover does. `nldd-sheet` always shows its bar.
0.26.0: **`nldd-text-editor` hides the formatting marks by default.** `syntax` now defaults to `"hidden"`: the marks of bold, italic, links and headings are hidden, a bullet is a dot and a quote a line, and the marks come back where the caret or selection touches them. The value stays plain markdown. Set `syntax="visible"` to keep the dimmed marks, for people who write markdown.

**`appearance` on `nldd-keyboard-shortcut` is now `keycap` or `text`, where it was `box` or `simple`.** The names say what you see: each key as a keycap, or the keys as plain text. The old values do nothing, and `nldd lint --fix` renames them (`keyboard-shortcut-appearance-renamed`). Keycaps no longer have a `+` between them, since they already stand apart.
0.25.0:
**A slot for text takes the element that carries it.** In `nldd-title`, `nldd-title-cell`, `nldd-text-cell` and `nldd-identity` a slot takes a `

` of your own, or a heading in the default slot of `nldd-title` and `nldd-title-cell`, with links, tags or `` inside it. The paragraph or heading is then in the HTML before any script runs. The component draws a plain box around what is in a slot, and no longer a `

` or heading of its own: text or an inline element straight in a slot loses its paragraph, and `heading-level` on `nldd-title-cell` only applies to `text`. Put plain text in the attribute, or wrap it in a `

` or heading. Two new rules report it as an error: `slot-needs-element` for an inline element, and `slot-text-needs-element` in the browser for plain text.

**`nldd-text` takes its text in a `

` or `` of your own, or plain text in `text`.** The slot takes a `

`, or a `` where the text is no paragraph, such as a number in a stat, with the inline elements inside it. What is in the slot is in the HTML the server sends; `text` draws a `

` in the browser, which is enough in an application. Text straight in `nldd-text` is no longer valid: the new rule `text-needs-element` reports it as an error, and `nldd lint --fix` wraps it in a `

`, so it stays in the HTML. The look of links, mentions, ``, `` and `` now comes from the global stylesheet: `text.css`, part of `global.css`. A page that loads only the component styles, or puts `nldd-text` in a shadow root of its own, needs `text.css` for that look: `@nldd/design-system/styles/text`.

**`nldd lint` reads `.js` files, also in a folder.** JSX in a `.js` file, as a React app with Create React App or Docusaurus writes it, is now checked like a `.jsx` file, where it reported `file-not-read`. A folder scan skipped `.js` altogether, so it now also checks Lit templates there, and reports `file-not-read` for markup in a plain string. Both can bring new findings. A minified bundle (`.min.js`, or a file with a line of 2,000 characters or more) is left out: check a build through its HTML.

**`nldd lint` reads MDX, and the prose of Markdown.** An `.mdx` file reported `file-not-read`; now the linter checks the components in its prose as well as in its code blocks, when you name the file. An expression in a value counts as bound, a spread as a spread, and `onClick`, `className` and `key` are read as JSX. In a `.md` file it now also checks the markup in the prose, not only the code blocks. A folder scan leaves both out, so a README or a docs site does not turn red unasked. Text that Markdown turns into a paragraph counts as one, so `text-needs-element` does not fire on it. Both can bring new findings. `--fix` works there too, and renames a tag in a mention such as `` `<nldd-app-view>` ``.
0.24.0: **`background="accent-tinted"` is gone from the page sections and `nldd-hero`.** A whole section in the accent tint drew too much attention and did not read well. Use `tinted`, or put the content that belongs to the service in an `nldd-card` or `nldd-box` with `background="accent-tinted"`, which keep it. `nldd lint` reports the old value.

**The translation keys `components.date-field.cancel-action` and `components.time-field.cancel-action` are gone,** now that the bottom sheet closes with "Klaar". An override of them no longer shows anywhere. `nldd lint` names `components.date-field.confirm-action` and `components.time-field.confirm-action` in their place.
0.23.0: **The old `sidebar` names on `nldd-navigation-split-view` are gone.** Use `primary-sidebar-as-sheet`, `primary-sidebar-accessible-label`, `slot="primary-sidebar"`, `showPrimarySidebarSheet()` and `hidePrimarySidebarSheet()`. `nldd lint --fix` renames the attributes and the slot; the two methods you rename yourself.

**`--semantics-buttons-inherit-filled-content-color` is removed.** The label of an `inherit-filled` button takes `--context-background-color`, so the token had no effect. `nldd lint` names that variable where you read the old one.
**`box` on `nldd-icon` is now `tile`.** It draws the icon on a tile, the square that shares its corner with an organization `nldd-avatar`. `nldd lint --fix` renames it.
**`--context-parent-background-color` is now `--context-background-color`.** It is the background of the nearest surface, not of the parent. `nldd lint` names the new name.

**What sits on a colored surface of your own takes its colors from the context, not from `color`.** The spinner, `color="content"` on `nldd-badge` and `nldd-avatar`, the mark of a `content` checkbox, radio button or switch, and the label of a `content-filled` button used to fall back to the text color or a computed contrast. They now read `--context-content-color` and `--context-background-color`, which default to the page colors. Set both on the element that paints the surface. The defaults resolve on `:root`, so a subtree that redefines `--semantics-content-*`, such as a local theme, sets the context there too.

**`color="inherit"` is now `color="content"`** on `nldd-avatar`, `nldd-badge`, `nldd-keyboard-shortcut`, `nldd-checkbox`, `nldd-radio-button`, `nldd-switch` and their fields. The value takes the content color of the context, not the CSS `color` around it. `nldd lint --fix` renames it.

**`color` is gone from `nldd-title` and `nldd-rich-text`, and `color="inherit"` from `nldd-text`.** Text takes the colors its surface passes on, so on the accent hero, in a tooltip or in a selected row it needs no attribute. Where your own CSS paints a surface and sets `color`, set `--context-content-color` with it, and the secondary and the three link colors where they differ. `nldd lint` reports the old attribute.

**`inherit-filled` and `inherit-tinted` are now `content-filled` and `content-tinted`** on `nldd-button`, `nldd-icon-button`, `nldd-split-button` and `nldd-button-bar`. They take their colors from `--context-content-color`, not the CSS `color` around them, like every other `content` value. `nldd lint --fix` renames them. Their tokens move with them, `inherit` becoming `content` in the name: `--semantics-buttons-inherit-tinted-background-color`, `--semantics-buttons-inherit-tinted-content-color`, `--semantics-buttons-inherit-tinted-content-secondary-color`, `--semantics-buttons-inherit-tinted-highlight-border-color`, `--semantics-buttons-inherit-tinted-divider-color`, `--semantics-buttons-inherit-filled-background-color`, `--semantics-buttons-inherit-filled-content-secondary-color`, `--semantics-buttons-inherit-filled-highlight-border-color`, `--semantics-buttons-inherit-filled-divider-color`. `nldd lint` names the new name where you read an old one.

**`nldd-icon` takes `--context-content-color` by default,** not the CSS `color` of its parent. Inside a component of the system nothing changes. In your own markup, set `--context-content-color` where you set `color`.

**The functional colors of `nldd-icon` are named as on `nldd-text`.** `color="primary-content"` is now `content`, the default, and `secondary-content` is now `secondary`. `nldd lint --fix` renames them.
0.22.0: **`nldd-title` takes its size from its level, and `size` takes `display-1` to `display-6` instead of a number.** An h2 looks like `display-2` without a `size` of its own, and so does an `<h2>` you put in the default slot. Set `size` where a heading should look smaller than its place, not a lower level. A title with a `heading-level` other than 3 and no `size` changes size: give it `size="display-3"` to keep the old look. `nldd lint --fix` renames the numbers to `display-n`, the same names as the display sizes of `nldd-text`.

**An `nldd-title` without a level shows as body text.** It was `display-3`, which made a paragraph look like a heading. A `size` or custom size does nothing without a level now. Give the title a `heading-level` or a heading in the slot, or use `nldd-text` with a display size for large letters that are not a heading. `nldd lint` finds these titles: `title-needs-heading-level` was a hint and is now a warning.

**`nldd-title-cell` takes `display-1` to `display-6` for `size` instead of a number,** like `nldd-title`. Its default stays `display-5`, and `display-6` in a table row: unlike a title, a cell does not take its size from `heading-level`, so every row in a list looks the same. `nldd lint --fix` renames the numbers.

**`nldd-text-editor` and `nldd-code-editor` have a frame by default, and `appearance` is gone.** An editor without `appearance` now gets the border, fill, padding and focus ring of the other input fields. For an editor inside a composition that provides those itself, such as a message field with its own toolbar, set the boolean `embedded`. `nldd lint --fix` replaces `appearance="simple"` with `embedded` and removes `appearance="input-field"`, which does nothing now. An editor that had no `appearance` and sits in a frame of its own needs `embedded` by hand, because the linter cannot tell it apart from one that should get the frame.

**`nldd-drag-handle-cell` is now `nldd-reorder-handle-cell`, and `reorderable-only` is now `reorder-handle`.** The names follow `reorderable` and `nldd-reorder` on the list. `reorder-handle` is an attribute of every cell now, so typed JSX accepts it, and it makes that cell the grip: an `nldd-cell` with a control of your own, or a cell without one. The cell shows only while the list is `reorderable`, as before. `nldd-reorder-handle-cell` carries the attribute by itself, so it needs nothing else. The translation key is `components.reorder-handle-cell.accessible-label`. `nldd lint --fix` renames the tag, its import and the attribute.

**Events have a plain name without `nldd-`, in kebab-case, like `change` and `close` on the platform.** Rename your listeners; `nldd lint` cannot find them, so search your code for the old names:
  | Component | Was | Is now |
  |---|---|---|
  | `nldd-list`, `nldd-document-tab-bar` | `nldd-reorder` | `reorder` |
  | `nldd-kanban` | `nldd-move`, `nldd-move-denied` | `move`, `move-denied` |
  | `nldd-tab-bar`, `nldd-document-tab-bar` | `tabchange` | `tab-change` |
  | `nldd-document-tab-bar` | `tabdismiss`, `tabempty` | `tab-dismiss`, `tab-empty` |
  | `nldd-one-time-code-field` | `nldd-complete` | `complete` |
  | `nldd-text-editor` | `nldd-text-editor-state`, `-mention`, `-typeahead`, `-annotation-click` | `state-change`, `mention`, `typeahead`, `annotation-click` |
  | `nldd-tooltip` | `nldd-tooltip-dismiss` | `dismiss` |
  | `nldd-just-in-time-education` | `nldd-close` | `close` |
  The `dismiss` of `nldd-tooltip` and the `close` of `nldd-just-in-time-education` no longer bubble, like `close` on a dialog: under their plain names they would reach an `nldd-banner`, `nldd-notification`, sheet or dialog around them, which fire the same name for themselves. Listen on the element itself.
0.21.0: **`nldd-dropdown` no longer sends a `change` of its own.** The native `change` of the slotted `<select>` bubbles on instead, so a listener on the select, on the dropdown or higher up hears it, a React `onChange` on the select included. It has no `detail`, and its `target` is the select, not the dropdown: replace `event.detail.value` with `event.target.value`, or read `value` on the dropdown, and compare `currentTarget` where you checked `target` against the dropdown.
0.20.0: **Content in a slot wins over the attribute for the same content.** Where a component takes both, such as `icon` and `slot="icon"`, or `text` and the default slot, the slot now shows and the attribute is what shows while the slot is empty. Before, the attribute won in `nldd-button`, `nldd-icon-button`, `nldd-toggle-button`, `nldd-segmented-control-item`, `nldd-tag`, `nldd-link`, `nldd-tab-bar-item`, `nldd-icon-cell`, `nldd-token`, `nldd-breadcrumbs-item`, `nldd-page-footer-legal-bar-item` and `nldd-step-bar-item`. Only markup that sets both notices; the new lint rule `slot-attribute-no-effect` finds it. Whitespace between the tags does not count as content.

**Components no longer write an attribute that only repeats the default,** such as `type="button"` on `nldd-button`, `size="16"` on `nldd-spacer`, `background="inherit"` on `nldd-page` or an empty `href=""` on `nldd-card`. The property still holds the value, so only code that selects on the attribute notices: read the property instead. `value` on `nldd-progress-bar` and `nldd-progress-circle` keeps its attribute.
**`nldd-button-group` and `nldd-button-bar` no longer write their defaults onto their buttons,** such as `size="md"` or `appearance="neutral-tinted"`. Another size or appearance is still written.
**`nldd-menu` no longer reflects `width`,** also not a width you set yourself. The width still applies. If you selected on `nldd-menu[width]`, use a class of your own instead.
0.19.0: **`search-button` on `nldd-search-field` takes `secondary` or `primary`,** the appearances of `nldd-button`, instead of `neutral-tinted` and `accent-filled`. They look the same as before. `nldd lint --fix` renames them.
0.18.0: **`nldd-column-board` and `nldd-column-board-column` are now `nldd-kanban` and `nldd-kanban-column`,** with the import path `@nldd/design-system/kanban`, the classes `NLDDKanban` and `NLDDKanbanColumn` and the translation keys `components.kanban.*`. The name fits a board whose columns are a team or a phase, not only tasks. There is no alias; `nldd lint --fix` renames the tags, imports and classes, also from the older `nldd-task-board`.

**`nldd-number-field` can be empty, and starts empty without a `value`.** It used to start at 0, so an optional field with `min="1"` that nobody touched made the form invalid, and an emptied field jumped back to its last number. Empty is now no answer: it submits an empty string, `min` and `max` judge only a number that was filled in, and the new `required` asks for a value. `value` and `detail.value` of `input` and `change` are `null` when the field is empty, so code that reads them as a number has to handle that. Give a field that should start at a number its `value`. From empty, + and - start at 0, or at the nearer end of the range when 0 lies outside it.
0.17.0: **`nldd-task-board` and `nldd-task-board-column` are now `nldd-column-board` and `nldd-column-board-column`,** with the import path `@nldd/design-system/column-board`, the classes `NLDDColumnBoard` and `NLDDColumnBoardColumn` and the translation keys `components.column-board.*`. A column can be a status, but also a team or a phase, and then "task" was the wrong word. There is no alias; `nldd lint --fix` renames the tags, imports and classes. The default accessible name of the board is now "Bord" instead of "Takenbord".

**`show-search-button` on `nldd-search-field` is now `search-button`,** which also takes the appearance of the button: `neutral-tinted` (also with no value, as before) or `accent-filled`, for a page where searching is the main task. `nldd lint --fix` renames it.
0.16.0: **The package needs Node 20.19 or newer.** The parsers of `nldd lint` moved to versions that only run there, so the linter no longer runs on Node 18, also not for `.vue`, `.html` and `.j2`. Reading `.tsx` and `.jsx` already asked for it. Node 18 and 20 are both out of support.

**The texts of the toggle on `nldd-password-field` are translation keys now, as on every other field.** The attributes `show-button-text`, `hide-button-text`, `show-button-accessible-label` and `hide-button-accessible-label` are gone, and `nldd lint` reports them as unknown. Move a text you set to `translations`, on the field or with `setTranslations()`:
  - `show-button-text` → `components.password-field.show-action` ("Toon")
  - `hide-button-text` → `components.password-field.hide-action` ("Verberg")
  - `show-button-accessible-label` → `components.password-field.show-accessible-label` ("Toon wachtwoord")
  - `hide-button-accessible-label` → `components.password-field.hide-accessible-label` ("Verberg wachtwoord")

**An `nldd-split-button` needs its menu.** The chevron opens an `nldd-menu` or `nldd-popover` in the `popup` slot, or the one `popovertarget` names, and `menu-click` is gone with the split button that had neither. A menu without `slot="popup"` still works, as the split button has no other slots, but `slot="popup"` is how it is written now, as on `nldd-button` and `nldd-icon-button`. `nldd lint` reports a split button without a menu.

**The chevron of an `nldd-split-button` says which action it belongs to:** "Meer opties voor Bewaar" instead of "Meer opties", so two split buttons in one bar no longer sound the same. The translation key `components.split-button.menu-action` is now `components.split-button.show-options-action`, with `{text}` for the label of the main action. Rename an override and add the placeholder.

**`appearance` on `nldd-split-button` takes its own values only:** `neutral-tinted`, `neutral-base`, `accent-filled`, `primary`, `secondary`, `inherit-tinted` and `inherit-filled`. The transparent and critical appearances of `nldd-button` were never styled for a split button, which needs a surface of its own to read as one control, and `nldd lint` now reports them.
0.15.0:
**9 translation keys are renamed, so the key names what the action does.** A key without a verb read as a choice. An override under an old key no longer applies, and the text falls back to Dutch. Rename it in your `translations`:
  - `components.date-picker.choose-month-action` → `components.date-picker.to-choose-month-action`, now "Maand kiezen", as it opens a list
  - `components.date-picker.choose-year-action` → `components.date-picker.to-choose-year-action`, now "Jaar kiezen"
  - `components.document-tab-bar.overflow-action` → `components.document-tab-bar.show-more-tabs-action`
  - `components.list.search-clear-action` → `components.list.clear-search-action`
  - `components.pagination.next-action` → `components.pagination.go-to-next-page-action`
  - `components.pagination.page-action` → `components.pagination.go-to-page-action`
  - `components.pagination.previous-action` → `components.pagination.go-to-previous-page-action`
  - `components.text-editor.code-copy-action` → `components.text-editor.copy-code-action`
  - `components.token-field.token-menu-action` → `components.token-field.open-token-menu-action`, now "Toon opties voor", as on `nldd-token`
0.14.0: **Warnings changed shape.** Tests that spy on `console.warn` for a text of this package need the new text: `[nldd] <rule>: ...`. Most warnings now arrive a moment later, once per element.
0.13.0: **Three translation keys are renamed** to say that their text starts in lowercase, because it is placed inside a longer string: `components.progress-bar.completed-suffix-text` and `components.progress-circle.completed-suffix-text` are now `…completed-suffix-lowercase-text`, and `components.date-picker.week-number-column-short-label` is now `…week-number-column-short-lowercase-label`. An override under the old key no longer applies; rename it.
0.12.0: **The icon alias `chart-line` is now `line-chart`**, next to the new `bar-chart` for `chart-bar-x-axis`. Replace `icon="chart-line"` with `icon="line-chart"`, or use the icon's own name, `chart-line-x-y-axis`.

**`--components-text-editor-mention-*` is now `--semantics-mentions-*`**, since the editor and the rich text share the mention colors. It adds a `highlight-border-color` for the edge and an `is-hovered` and `is-active` background for a mention that is a link. The themes that ship with the system moved along. A theme of your own that sets the old names loses its mention colors without an error, so rename them.
0.11.0: **`--components-tab-bar-is-current-*` is now `--semantics-tabs-is-current-*`.** `nldd-document-tab-bar` reads the same tokens for its selected document, so two components share them. If your theme sets these tokens, rename them.

**`--primitives-color-accent-*` is the theme color in every theme.** In rood, robijnrood and oranje the accent scale used to be gray, and in geel and donkergeel its dark steps were near-black in light mode. Those choices now sit in the semantics and components tokens that need them, and every component reads such a token instead of the scale. If your own CSS reads `--primitives-color-accent-*`, it now gets the theme color in those themes; read a semantics token to follow what the theme decides.

**The `indicator` slot of `nldd-activity-indicator` is gone.** The activity indicator is for loading of unknown length; a progress bar or circle in its slot lost the label and announced itself twice. When you know the progress, show `nldd-progress-bar` or `nldd-progress-circle` directly instead of inside the activity indicator.
0.10.0: **`nldd-badge` no longer takes a Rijkshuisstijl color.** `color` is the same set as `nldd-status-bar`, plus `inherit`: `critical` (the default), `accent`, `neutral`, `warning`, `success` and `inherit`. A badge is a signal, not a category, and a color of its own clashed with the theme. A badge with `color="hemelblauw"` or another named color now gets the accent, and says so in the console during development. Pick the color for the whole site with a theme, or use `custom-color` for a color of its own.

**`nldd-hero` no longer takes a Rijkshuisstijl color for its panel.** `main-background` is `accent` (the default) or `base`. A color per hero came before themes. A theme now picks the color for the whole site. A hero with `main-background="donkerblauw"` or another named color gets the accent instead, and says so in the console during development. To keep the color, set the theme on `<html>` (`data-nldd-theme="donkerblauw"`, with `@nldd/design-system/themes/donkerblauw.css`) and remove the attribute. Without a theme the accent is lintblauw.
0.9.0: **The translation key for the new-tab hint is renamed.** `components.{name}.opens-in-new-tab-label` is now `components.{name}.link-hint-new-tab-lowercase-label`, next to the new `link-hint-external-lowercase-label` and `link-hint-external-new-tab-lowercase-label`, so the three hints of a link sit together. The text always follows a name after a comma, so the default is lowercase: "opent in nieuw tabblad". If you override this text with `translations` or `setTranslations()`, rename the key and write the text in lowercase. The old key does nothing anymore.
0.8.100: **Items in a horizontal-scroll `nldd-collection` stop at 480px.** One or two items that fit grew to the full width of the container, so a card of 320px became more than 1000px wide on a desktop. They now grow up to 480px and stay at the start. An `item-min-width` wider than 480px raises the limit with it, and `item-max-width` sets your own; `item-max-width="100%"` brings back the old behavior.

**`item-width` on `nldd-collection` is now `item-min-width`.** It was a minimum in every layout: in a grid the narrowest a column gets, in a horizontal scroll the width an item never shrinks below. The new name says so, and pairs with `item-max-width`. There is no alias. An `item-width` left on a collection does nothing, so its items fall back to the default of 280px; in development the collection says so once, with the renamed attribute. Rename the attribute on every `nldd-collection`.
0.8.99: **`label` on `nldd-toolbar` is now `accessible-label`.** It was the one place where an accessible name was called `label`; every other component says `accessible-label`, and on `nldd-toolbar-item` `label` is the visible text below the item, which made the two easy to mix up. There is no alias: a `label` left on a toolbar does nothing, so the toolbar loses its name. Rename the attribute on every `nldd-toolbar`. The `label` on `nldd-toolbar-item` stays as it is.
0.8.98: **Rules in `nldd-validation-list` skip an empty value unless the field needs one.** An empty value used to fail `match`, `minlength` and `maxlength` like any other. It now passes them, the way the native `pattern` and `minlength` leave an empty input alone, unless an item has `required` or the control itself is `required`. If you counted on `minlength` to stop an empty field, add `required` to the control or add an item with `required`. For example: `<nldd-validation-item id="password-required" required>Vul een wachtwoord in</nldd-validation-item>` next to the `minlength` item.
0.8.97: **`main-width` on `nldd-hero` follows the content.** `1/2`, `2/3` and `3/4` are gone: half the width was too narrow for text on md, and three quarters too wide to read on a large screen. The panel is now as wide as its content needs, between 480px and 640px and never wider than the image allows (`main-width="auto"`, the default). `full` stays, and any CSS width (`560px`, `60%`) sets it exactly, still never wider than the image allows. A fraction is not a CSS width, so it falls back to `auto` and says so in development.

**A hero with an image overlaps by default.** `nldd-hero` used to keep its text panel on the image; it now lets it fall over the bottom edge and run on below, and takes only the horizontal side of `main-position`. A hero whose panel stands at the top or along a side (`top-left`, `left` and so on), or whose panel is too short to reach below the image, needs `layout="contained"` to stay as it was. A hero without an image does not change.

**`nldd-app-view` is now `nldd-shell`.** It is the outer layer of everything, a website as much as an application, and "app view" suggested it was only for the second. Rename the tag in every page, the import (`@nldd/design-system/app-view` becomes `/shell`) and the class (`NLDDAppView` becomes `NLDDShell`). There is no alias: an `nldd-app-view` left behind is an unknown element, so the page loses its background and its scroll mode, and the document font, which the stylesheet sets once a shell is on the page. A CSS selector on `nldd-app-view` needs the new name too.

**`data-width` in `nldd-rich-text` is now `data-rich-text-width`.** The attribute that moves one child to another width zone (`main`, `wide` or `full`) said neither what it belonged to nor that it only works inside a rich text, and it read like the `width` of a page section, which is something else. There is no alias: a `data-width` left behind does nothing, and the child falls back to the zone of its kind.

**`is-last` is gone from page sections.** `nldd-page` marks the section that takes the leftover height with `data-growing` instead of the `is-last` class, since a framework's class binding rewrites `class` and could wipe it. If you styled `.is-last` yourself, use `[data-growing]`.
0.8.96:
**`nldd-step-indicator` is now `nldd-step-bar`, and `nldd-timeline-track-cell` is now `nldd-step-cell`.** They are one family, the steps of a process across and under each other, as `nldd-progress-bar` and `nldd-progress-circle` are one family for how much is done. "Timeline" said less than the cell does: most of all it draws steps. Rename the tags, and the classes and imports if you use them:
  | Was | Now |
  |---|---|
  | `nldd-step-indicator`, `NLDDStepIndicator` | `nldd-step-bar`, `NLDDStepBar` |
  | `nldd-step-indicator-item`, `NLDDStepIndicatorItem` | `nldd-step-bar-item`, `NLDDStepBarItem` |
  | `nldd-timeline-track-cell`, `NLDDTimelineTrackCell` | `nldd-step-cell`, `NLDDStepCell` |
  | `@nldd/design-system/step-indicator` | `@nldd/design-system/step-bar` |
  | `@nldd/design-system/timeline-track-cell` | `@nldd/design-system/step-cell` |
  | translation keys `components.step-indicator.*` | `components.step-bar.*` |
  The attributes stay the same. An old tag is an unknown element now and renders nothing, without a warning, so search your markup.

**The `--components-*` custom properties no longer exist.** If you set or read one, nothing happens now, without a warning. Most were never meant to be touched. The ones that more components share moved to semantics:
  | Was | Now |
  |---|---|
  | `--components-code-viewer-token-*-color` | `--semantics-code-syntax-*-color` |
  | `--components-list-item-is-*`, `--components-list-item-indicator-*` | `--semantics-list-items-is-*`, `--semantics-list-items-indicator-*` |
  | `--components-menu-bar-item-inline-padding` | `--semantics-menu-bar-items-inline-padding` |
  | `--components-menu-box-shadow` | `--semantics-overlays-box-shadow` |
  | `--components-menu-item-is-highlighted-background-color` / `-content-color` | `--semantics-controls-is-highlighted-indicator-color` / `-contrast-color` |
  Search your own CSS for `--components-` to find what this affects.
0.8.95: **The current step in `nldd-step-indicator` is `status="current"` on the step.** It was a number on the parent (`current="2"`), which pointed at the wrong step as soon as an app left one out. Now it is the same `status` a step already had, with the same three values as `nldd-timeline-track-cell`: `current` marks where you are and the parent derives the rest from it, while `past` and `future` stay an exception for one step. With no step marked, step 1 is current, and with more than one the last wins. Move the attribute: `<nldd-step-indicator current="2">` becomes `status="current"` on the second item. A leftover `current` on the parent no longer does anything, and a dev build says so in the console, also when a framework sets it later.

**The long form of a skill name is `/nldd-design-system:nldd-design`**, no longer `/nldd:nldd-design`, because the prefix follows the plugin name. This holds for existing installs too, from their next update. A permission rule such as `Skill(nldd:nldd-design-build)` or a hook that matches on the long form stops matching, without an error. The short form (`/nldd-design`) is unchanged, and so is the skill an assistant picks by itself. The README has a search that finds the places to change.
0.8.94: **`variant` is now `appearance` on `nldd-button`, `nldd-button-bar`, `nldd-icon-button`, `nldd-split-button`, `nldd-keyboard-shortcut`, `nldd-code-viewer`, `nldd-code-editor`, `nldd-text-editor` and `nldd-list`.** The values stay the same, so `variant="primary"` becomes `appearance="primary"`, and the property is `appearance` too. `variant` meant two different things across the system: how something is drawn, and what kind of thing it is. On these nine it was always the first, a designed style with its color included, so it now has a name of its own. `variant` stays on the components where it says what kind of thing it is and sets the icon and role with it, such as `nldd-banner`, `nldd-notification`, `nldd-status-bar` and `nldd-inline-dialog`. A `variant` left on one of the nine is ignored without a warning and the component falls back to its default style, so search your markup for it. The exported types follow: `CodeViewerVariant`, `CodeEditorVariant`, `TextEditorVariant`, `ListVariant` and the `Variant` of `nldd-icon-button` are now `CodeViewerAppearance`, `CodeEditorAppearance`, `TextEditorAppearance`, `ListAppearance` and `Appearance`.

**`variant` on `nldd-timeline-track-cell` is now `level`.** `major`, `minor` and `none` say how far down the hierarchy a row sits: `minor` is a row that belongs under the one above it. The values stay the same, so `variant="minor"` becomes `level="minor"`.

**`mode` on `nldd-progress-bar` and `nldd-progress-circle` is now `variant`.** `progress` and `distribution` are two kinds of indicator, progress toward a goal and the parts of a whole, and the screen reader hears something different for each, which is what `variant` stands for in this system. The values stay the same, so `mode="distribution"` becomes `variant="distribution"`. The types `ProgressBarMode` and `ProgressCircleMode` are now `ProgressBarVariant` and `ProgressCircleVariant`.
0.8.93: **The page sections no longer take `scheme`.** `nldd-simple-section`, `nldd-full-bleed-section`, `nldd-hero`, `nldd-sidebar-section` and the two- and three-column sections could pin `light`, `dark` or `inverted` on a band, which made one section decide the color scheme for everything inside it. A section still draws its surface with `background`, which is what the components inside read; light and dark stay a choice for the page, through `color-scheme` on a root element. `nldd-window` keeps its own `scheme`.

**`nldd-button-group` follows its own width, and that is its default.** `orientation` was `horizontal` or `vertical`, with `vertical` as the default, so every group that did not say otherwise stacked its buttons at every width. It now takes `auto` as well, and that is the new default: a row, and stacked over the full width once the group itself is narrower than the sm breakpoint. The group is its own container query, so the same group is a row in a page and a stack in a sheet beside it, without a media query of yours. A group that wants to keep stacking everywhere says `orientation="vertical"`. A stacked group stretches the buttons through `--context-button-width`, which `nldd-button` now reads, so a button follows the parent that stacks it without anyone setting `width="full"`. The group used to write that attribute onto its children and take it off again; it no longer touches them, so CSS or a test of yours that keys on `[width="full"]` inside a group stops matching.

**The skills are now `nldd-design`, `nldd-design-build`, `nldd-design-migrate`, `nldd-design-upgrade` and `nldd-design-contribute`.** `nldd` meant four things at once: the organization, the npm package, the plugin and the skill inside it, so the name said nothing about what the skill was for and its description had to carry an anti-trigger instead. The names now say the task. What is shared between them, the component reference, the changelog and the design guidelines, moves to `nldd-design`: that is reference material whether you are building something new or converting something old, and a migration needs it as much as a new app does.
  **Raising the version of an app that already runs on this system is its own skill**, `nldd-design-upgrade`. It sat as a section inside the build skill, which is the wrong place twice over: an upgrade is not building something new, and it is not a migration either, so whichever of the two you reached for, the guidance was in the other one. It matters here more than in most systems because this project releases everything as a patch, including a breaking change, so the version number tells you nothing about whether a jump is safe. That is a deliberate choice in `.releaserc.json`, not how semantic-release behaves by default, which makes it easy to assume the usual semver signal is there when it is not.
  **A skill named `nldd` stays behind to catch the old name**, and does nothing but point at the ones that replaced it. It is deliberately findable by the model and not just by `/nldd`, because the reference that breaks most quietly is a line in your own `CLAUDE.md` saying "use the nldd skill": nobody types anything there, so a slash command would not catch it. **It is removed after 1 March 2027**, so update your references rather than lean on it.
  **The plugin is still called `nldd`.** Installing it does not change, and `enabledPlugins` and `extraKnownMarketplaces` point at `nldd@nldd-plugins`, the plugin, so leave those alone.
  What to check, quietest first, because the first two give you no error at all:
  1. **The skill name in your own instruction files**: `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/*.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or the body of a skill of your own that says "use the nldd skill". Claude reads the instruction, does not find the skill, and carries on without it. Nothing warns; the output is just worse.
  2. **The skill name in subagent definitions** (`.claude/agents/*.md`) **and in hooks that match on it.** Equally silent.
  3. **`Skill(nldd)` in permission rules.** It stops matching, so you get a permission prompt where you had none.
  4. **Scripts or CI that call `claude -p "/nldd ..."`.** Since Claude Code 2.1.273 an unknown slash command is no longer a free deterministic rejection but a model call that answers with a "did you mean" text, so a script checking the exit code still sees 0 and now gets billed, variable output instead of a fixed error.
  5. **Typing `/nldd` interactively.** The loudest and least harmful.
  Invoke a skill either way: `/nldd-design-build` is the short form, and `/nldd:nldd-design-build` always resolves to ours even when a skill of your own carries the same name.

**The `subtitle` slot of `nldd-title` is now `supporting-text`.** That is what the text under a title is called in every other component, including `nldd-top-title-bar`. Rename `slot="subtitle"` to `slot="supporting-text"`, or use the new `supporting-text` attribute for plain text. Content still in `slot="subtitle"` is not shown, and in development the console says once which rename it needs.

**`nldd-form-section` calls its supporting text `supporting-text` throughout.** The span in the legend is now `.form-section__supporting-text` instead of `.form-section__subtitle`, and its token `--semantics-forms-section-supporting-text-font` instead of `--semantics-forms-section-subtitle-font`. The attribute already had that name. Rename the class in your CSS and the token where you override it: the old ones do nothing any more, without a warning.

**`nldd-page` in a split-view pane no longer carries the document's landmarks.** A page carries them: its header is the banner, its content the main landmark, its footer the contentinfo. A document has one of each, so two pages beside each other were two of each, which is invalid HTML that nothing on screen gives away. A page in a pane of a navigation, side-by-side or stacked split view, or inside an overlay, now renders a section and a plain div instead, which drops all three at once: a header inside sectioning content is no longer a banner.
  **Set `landmarks="page"` on the page in the pane that holds your primary content**, because only the application knows which pane that is. Nothing warns when you do not: the app shell simply has no main landmark, and a screen reader user loses the jump to the content. Give the other panes an `accessible-label` and they are named regions instead, which is a landmark worth having. `landmarks` also takes `region` to step down anywhere else, and a second page that still renders a main says so in development.

**`nldd-icon` takes `icon` instead of `name`.** Every other component that renders an icon already called it `icon`, so you had to remember the one exception. Rename `name="…"` to `icon="…"` on every `nldd-icon`. An icon that still has `name` draws the dashed placeholder circle, and in development the console says once which rename it needs.

**The `--components-title-*` tokens are gone.** `--components-title-{sm,md,lg}-overline-font` and `--components-title-{sm,md,lg}-subtitle-font` stood in `variables.css`, but `nldd-title` never read them, so overriding one changed nothing. The overline and the supporting text take `--primitives-font-body-sm-regular-tight` and `--primitives-font-body-md-regular-tight`. The two names are removed rather than renamed, so a `var()` of your own that points at one resolves to nothing.
0.8.87: **`label` and `detail` on a mention candidate are `text` and `supportingText`.** The words the rest of the system uses: `text` on a button, a menu item and a title cell, and `supporting-text` under it on a button and a title cell. `MentionCandidate` is `{ id, text, supportingText? }` now, and `nldd-text-editor-mention` carries `text` instead of `label`. The typeahead candidates use the same names.

**`modeless` is gone from `nldd-sheet` and `nldd-window`.** Both are always modal now: they open with `showModal()`, draw a backdrop and hold focus. The attribute promised an overlay you could leave open while working behind it, and the native `<dialog>` gives you the shell for that but none of the things that make it usable. Nothing in this system set it on either one, and the sheet's own story warned in its text that it did not lay out correctly. Whatever it was reaching for wants solving on its own terms rather than as a flag on a component built to be modal. `nldd-window` is still the positionable overlay: `top`, `left`, `right`, `bottom`, `centered`, `width` and `height` are what set it apart from `nldd-modal-dialog`, not this.

**`timing="default"` is now `timing="delay"`.** On `nldd-tooltip` (a 700ms show delay) and on `nldd-activity-indicator` (a 1000ms anti-flash delay), and on the `tooltip-timing` of `nldd-avatar` and `nldd-icon-button`, which forward it. A value named for its position in the list says nothing about what it does, and it breaks the day the default moves. Beside `instant` and `never`, `delay` is the only word that says when the thing appears, which is what those two already do. Which value is the default lives in the component, and an attribute equal to the default is dropped from the DOM anyway, so leaving it out and writing it are the same thing.

**`color="default"` on `nldd-avatar` is now `color="neutral"`.** Same reason. Not `neutral-tinted`: that fill is neutral-100 in light and neutral-300 in dark, where the shared neutral-tinted family is 75/200 on buttons and 50/150 on categories, so the name would promise a scale it is not on.

**`color` says `content` on `nldd-title`, `nldd-rich-text`, `nldd-text`, `nldd-text-cell`, `nldd-title-cell` and `nldd-icon-cell`.** On the first two the attribute had one value, `inherit`, and leaving it off meant the system's own text colors. Nameless, so the story control had to invent a word for the empty option and landed on `(auto)`, which sat in the same dropdown as `inherit` and read as a second way of saying "take it from somewhere else". They are opposites: `content` is the system's color, `inherit` is the surface's. Both are words now and there is nothing left to label. On `nldd-text` and the three cells that same color was called `default`, which said where it sat in the list rather than what it did, next to `secondary`, `accent`, `success`, `warning` and `critical` that all say what they are. They share one color scale and are read side by side in a row, so they move together. `content` is the word the tokens already use, as in `--semantics-content-color` and the `primary-content` of `nldd-icon`.

**`size` on `nldd-link` defaults to `inherit`.** Leaving it off already behaved as `inherit`: the CSS gives `:host(:not([size]))` and `:host([size="inherit"])` the same rules, and the story had a row saying so out loud. But the property held no value at all, so the control offered `(geen)` and `inherit` as two entries for one behavior, and reading `size` back gave `undefined`. Now it says what it does. Nothing renders differently.

**`size` on `nldd-avatar` and `nldd-icon` defaults to `full` instead of an empty string.** `full` was already implemented on both, already in the type and already documented as the default. Only the property disagreed. Nothing renders differently. Read `size` back and you now get `full` where you got `''`.
0.8.86: **A CSS length in `gap` on `nldd-collection` no longer applies.** It was the only component that took one. Use the step with the same number: `gap="16px"` becomes `gap="16"`. A gap that has to change with the viewport is `sm-gap` / `md-gap` / `lg-gap` rather than a length.

**`--context-layer-top` and `--context-layer-bottom` are now `--context-inset-top` and `--context-inset-bottom`.** The value says how much of the edge is taken by chrome that a sticky element has to clear, and layer reads as stacking order, which is what `z-index` and `@layer` are for. Inset is the word the platform already uses for this, as in `env(safe-area-inset-top)` and Android's window insets, and the same number is what `scroll-padding-top` wants, which has nothing sticky about it. Rename it wherever your app publishes or reads it. A CSS variable that no longer exists fails without a word, so nothing warns: sticky content lands against the top edge instead of below your bar. `nldd-app-view`, `nldd-page`, `nldd-sheet`, `nldd-bar-split-view` and `nldd-modal-dialog` all speak the new name.
0.8.84: **`error-message` on an input is now `unmet`, and there is no fallback.** It names the ids of the items a value does not satisfy, which is what an `nldd-validation-list` reads. Consumers replace the attribute wherever they set it, bound forms included: Angular's `[attr.error-message]` becomes `[attr.unmet]`. Nothing warns. `nldd-form-field` reads an attribute that is not there, so every message on the page silently stops appearing. One search and replace on `error-message`, minding that `error-message-ids` is a different, internal thing and keeps its name.

**`nldd-form-field-error-text` is gone.** An error you have to fix is a requirement the value does not meet, so it belongs in an `nldd-validation-list` beside the requirements that state themselves. Migration is per field and the ids travel with the texts: `<nldd-form-field-error-text id="password-length">Must be at least 8 characters.</nldd-form-field-error-text>` becomes `<nldd-validation-item id="password-length" minlength="8">At least 8 characters</nldd-validation-item>`, and anything only a server can decide becomes an item without a rule, still named in `unmet`. Leaving the old element in place is worse than a blank: an undefined custom element has no shadow styles, so every message renders permanently. Search for the tag; nothing warns.

**Validation texts are the requirement, not the instruction.** The same line does two jobs, a requirement up front and, once the field is judged, what is still wrong. So "Use at least 8 characters" becomes "At least 8 characters", "Pick at least one option" becomes "At least one option", and "Enter a valid company number (8 digits)" becomes "A company number of 8 digits". This touches every message a consumer has written; the examples are in `skills/nldd/SKILL.md`.

**An empty `nldd-list` or `nldd-table` says nothing of its own.** `empty-text` and `empty-supporting-text` are gone from both, and with them the default `nldd-inline-dialog` they fed. What an empty list means is the app's to write: "no assets yet" and "nothing matched that search" are different sentences with different next moves. Measured in the two applications that lean on this system hardest: 324 of their 330 lists set neither the attributes nor the slot, so all of them fell back on the same Dutch "Geen items" in an English interface, while 62 inline dialogs stood beside those lists in the consumer's own markup because the slot was never found. Put an `nldd-inline-dialog` in `[slot="empty"]`, which already worked and is now the only way. Empty with that slot unfilled, both take themselves off the page rather than drawing an empty surface: on a boxed list that was a tinted bar with nothing in it, which reads as a skeleton that never loaded, and it made "nothing" look different per variant. They warn once in development instead, so a blank area becomes a question to whoever is building rather than a silence for whoever is reading. `nldd-menu` keeps its default: a filter that matches nothing is a state of the control, not content of the app.

**`nldd-timeline-track-cell` splits `variant`, `minor` and `status` into `size`, `variant` and `status`.** `variant="dot|step"` set the dot and the lane at once, `minor` sat beside it, and `status="none"` took the dot away from a list of values that is otherwise about progress, so a row without a dot lost the lane it had to stand in. Map `variant="step"` to `size="md"`, `minor` to `variant="minor"`, and `status="none"` to `variant="none"` plus the status that fits. `size` is `sm` (16px) or `md` (24px), and a number fits in `md`.

**`selected` on `nldd-tab-bar-item` is now `current`.** The name every other navigation component uses: `nldd-menu-bar-item`, `nldd-breadcrumbs` and, since 0.8.83, `nldd-list-item`. A bar that switches content still renders `aria-selected` and a `navigation` bar `aria-current="page"`, and it was that second mode where the old name was wrong. Rename one attribute per bar. The old one does nothing, and warns in dev. `nldd-document-tab-bar-item` keeps `selected`, because those are tabs over documents rather than routes.
0.8.83: **`database-disabled` and `database-unavailable` are now `disabled-database` and `unavailable-database`.** The set puts the state in front everywhere else: `new-namespace`, `no-priority`, `checked-small`. Those two trailed it, and were the only aliases that did apart from the `-light` weights, which name the drawing rather than a state. Both still point at `cylinder-split-slash`. Consumers on an old name change one string.

**`nldd-list-item-action` is now `nldd-list-item-segment`.** The component was not always an action: without `href`, `button` or `checkbox`, and inside a listbox, it renders as a plain container. What it always is, is a piece of the row with its own hit area and its own fill, which is what the docs had been calling it all along. Consumers rename the element and the import path, and the attributes stay the same. The host classes follow: `has-leading-segment` and `has-trailing-segment`.

**Every list answers to the arrow keys, and `arrow-navigation` is gone.** Whether the arrow keys work is what a reader may assume about every list, not a setting per list, and as a setting it was unknowable from the outside. Consumers drop the attribute. Leaving it in does nothing, and warns in dev.

**`nldd-box` paints with `background`, like every other surface.** The attribute was `variant`, which in this system is the word for what a component is, not for which surface it draws. `nldd-app-view`, `nldd-page`, `nldd-split-view-pane` and `nldd-card` all call that `background`. So `variant="base|tinted|critical"` is now `background="base|tinted|critical"`. One thing to know: a box starts on `tinted` where a card starts on `base`, because a box stands out from the page and a card sits on it. Consumers change one string per box.

**The plus badges are named after what they make.** `add-namespace` is now `new-namespace`, `add-k8s` and `add-kubernetes` are `new-k8s` and `new-kubernetes`, and `add-text-document` is gone in favor of `new-text-document`. A namespace, a cluster and a document are made, not added. `add` stays for putting something that exists into something else, which is why `add-plugin`, `add-user`, `add-location` and `add-emoji` are unchanged. Consumers on an old name change one string.
0.8.80: **`nldd-box` draws its surface from one attribute.** `background="tinted|base"` and `variant="default|critical"` were two attributes for three states, and `critical` silently overruled `background`, so `background="base" variant="critical"` was a spelling whose first half did nothing. It is now `variant="tinted" | "base" | "critical"`, with `tinted` the default. Rename `background="base"` to `variant="base"`, drop `background="tinted"` (it is the default), and leave `variant="critical"` as it is. `variant="default"` becomes `variant="tinted"`.

**`nldd-list` does the same.** `background` only ever applied to `variant="box"` and did nothing under `simple`, which the documentation had to say out loud. The three states are now values of one attribute: `variant="simple" | "box-tinted" | "box-base"`. Rename `variant="box"` to `variant="box-tinted"` and `variant="box" background="base"` to `variant="box-base"`. Each value says what you get, so nobody has to know which fill `box` defaulted to.

**`no-dividers` is now `dividers`, and it can also say `on-touch`.** A pointer has the hover highlight to tell one row from the next, and a finger has nothing, so the line earns its place in the one case and is clutter in the other. That is a third state, and a second boolean beside `no-dividers` would have been the same two-attributes-for-three-states knot as above. It is now `dividers="always" | "on-touch" | "never"`, with `always` the default. Rename `no-dividers` to `dividers="never"`. `on-touch` hides the lines and brings them back under `(pointer: coarse)`, so a consumer no longer routes a viewport signal of its own into the list for this. Width was the wrong signal anyway: a narrow window on a laptop is still a mouse.

**`nldd-code-viewer` merges its two as well.** Same split as the two above: `background` applied only to `variant="box"` and the controls panel had to hide it the rest of the time. It is now `variant="box-tinted" | "box-base" | "simple"`, with `box-tinted` the default. Drop `variant="box"` (it is the default), rename `variant="box" background="base"` to `variant="box-base"`, and leave `variant="simple"` as it is.

**The `actions` slot of `nldd-title` is now `end`.** A title's trailing slot is a place, not a kind of content: a button fits there, and so do a menu, a status badge and a version number. Naming it after actions made every non-action in it read as a mistake. Rename `slot="actions"` to `slot="end"` on whatever you put beside a title. The `actions` slot of `nldd-banner`, `nldd-inline-dialog` and `nldd-modal-dialog` keeps its name: those really are action areas.

**The transport icons carry a `media-` prefix.** `play`, `play-filled`, `pause`, `pause-filled`, `stop`, `stop-filled`, `play-pause` and `play-pause-filled` are now `media-play` and so on, joining `media-backward` and `media-forward` which already had it. The old names keep working as aliases, so nothing breaks; they are simply not where the family lives any more.

**`nldd-byline` is now `nldd-identity`.** Same component, a name that says what it shows: a person or a group of people with their name and a supporting line, wherever that is useful, rather than only under an article. Rename the tag, the class (`NLDDByline` becomes `NLDDIdentity`) and the import path (`content/byline/byline.js` becomes `content/identity/identity.js`).

The group owns the overlap and the ring, which identity used to draw itself, so both components say one thing each.

**`nldd-box` no longer has padding of its own.** It draws the surface and nothing else, exactly as `nldd-card` already did, so one component owns the inset wherever it is used. Wrap what is inside in an `nldd-container` and let that set it: `<nldd-box><nldd-container padding="16">…</nldd-container></nldd-box>` reproduces the old look. Without it, content now sits against the border. The token that held the old value, `--components-box-padding`, is still there as the reference for what "16" means here.

**`nldd-banner`** — the two size-dependent custom properties carry their size in the name: `--components-banner-padding` becomes `--components-banner-md-padding` and `--components-banner-icon-size` becomes `--components-banner-md-icon-size`. Without the size segment they read as "the padding of every banner" while `sm` has its own value, and every other component names them this way. `--components-banner-corner-radius` and `--components-banner-content-color` are unchanged, because they do not differ per size. **`@nldd/design-system/tokens` is gone.** It only ever re-exported `breakpoints`, so import from `@nldd/design-system/breakpoints` instead. Same values, same names.

**The four `--primitives-font-family-*-fallback` variables are gone.** Nothing read them, so overriding one to drop RijksSans changed nothing while looking like the switch you were after. To use a different font, override `--primitives-font-family-sans-serif` and `--primitives-font-family-monospace` — or import `/styles/system-font` and skip the `@font-face` rules entirely.

The old names are gone. The aliases `text-documents`, `directories`, `tags` and `labels` moved along and keep working.
**`stack-text` is now `rectangle-stack-text`** (with new artwork), naming the shape it draws the way `rectangle-stack` already does.
**`house-and-appartment-building` is now `house-apartment-building`** (with new artwork) — the spelling fixed to match `apartment-building`, and the "and" dropped from the compound.

**`square-and-arrow-down` is now `square-arrow-down`**, dropping the "and" the way `square-arrow-up` and `square-arrow-right-top` already read. The aliases `save` and `import` moved along and keep working.

**The media-transport icons carry a `media-` prefix**: `backward`, `forward` and their `-filled`, `-end`, `-end-filled`, `-frame` and `-frame-filled` variants are now `media-backward`, `media-forward` and so on (12 renames). The bare names were ambiguous — "forward" reads as navigation more often than as media transport — and the icon `forward` was unreachable outright, shadowed by the alias `forward` → `chevron-right` (aliases win on resolution). That alias stays, as the counterpart of `back` → `chevron-left`. `play`, `pause`, `stop` and `play-pause` keep their names: they collide with nothing and are clear as they are.

The hover and selection fill of an interactive row is now genuinely clickable across the full painted width.

Segmented actions now own a fixed inline padding and are at least as wide as the row's control size (md 44px, sm 32px), so the hit area is a square at minimum. Remove spacer cells you added inside one for room or hit area — the action handles that itself now, and leaving them in doubles the space. Icon-only actions (a chevron in a tree) get slightly wider. An action at a row edge shifts 8px towards that edge, so its outer edge lands exactly where a row-wide action's hit area begins and its contents sit on the same grid as the text of an ordinary row. It shifts, it does not grow: the width stays the control size. If you reserve the chevron zone on leaf rows in a tree, watch rows without an indent spacer in front — there a branch row's action shifts along and the zone sits 8px further out. An action mid-row is unaffected.

**The serif tokens are gone.** `--primitives-font-family-serif` and `-serif-fallback` pointed at `RijksoverheidSerif`, a font the system does not ship and no component used. If you referenced them, set your own stack.

**Two icons renamed.** `rectangle-chevron-left-forward-slash-chevron-right` is now `chevron-left-forward-slash-chevron-right-rectangle`, so the shape it sits in comes last, the way the other names read. **`nldd-hero`** — the `media-corner` attribute is renamed to `media-corner-position` (freeing the `media-corner` namespace for the new media attributes).

**`nldd-list-item` translation key** `components.list-item.opens-in-new-tab-label` was renamed to `components.list-item.opens-in-new-tab-text`; update any `translations` override.

**`nldd-bar-split-view`** — dividers are now placed automatically wherever the main pane meets an adjacent bar (directly above and/or below it), at every breakpoint including `sm`, and never between two stacked bars on the same side. Root-owned registry drives chain collapse instead of walking stale parent links: fixes anchor-click not closing after multiple navigations and bounce-back to root.
